title: Generated item
description: SNG-296 / WORK ORDER v2 Track C. A generated piece of gear. ⚠️ THE MECHANICAL HOOK IS `bonusTags`, not `effects` — the consumer map records that 19/19 authored valley items carry neither an `effect` nor an `effects` field: gear resolves through `bonusTags` (inventory.js:equipmentBonus and wieldBonusFor), and only CONSUMABLES resolve through `effects`. An item generated without bonusTags is a name — exactly the failure the born-whole contract exists to prevent.

id.description: catalog key; without it an inventory entry can never be re-linked to its bonuses (inventory.js:37)

kind.description: ⚠️ `shield` is new here. The catalog has ZERO shields at HEAD while guard-shaped crafts are 19 of the defensive logics — Aevi's finding, and the reason the enum names it explicitly rather than letting shields hide under `armor`. `relic` (SNG-658): a substrate-charged find (keystone shard, snarl bead, the far token), carried for its charge; its bonusTags still hook rolls.

bonusTags.description: THE MECHANICAL HOOK. Matched against an action's tags by equipmentBonus (ordinary rolls) and wieldBonusFor (skill-battle rounds). Empty means the item cannot affect any roll.

tradition.description: whose people made it — the grammar Aevi authors keys on this, so an ashwarden blade reads ashwarden

worth.description: a band, not a price — there is no pricing engine

provenance.description: where it came from, so a found thing has a history

effects.description: CONSUMABLES ONLY. Gear does not use this — see the description above. ⛑ SNG-658: an OBJECT of numeric pools, e.g. { energy: 10 } or { health: 8 }, because that is what every reader takes (encounters.js restores from fx.energy / fx.health, inventory.js reads item.effects || {}, app.js lists Object.entries). The earlier 'array' type described a shape nothing reads.

substrateCharge.description: relics only: the substrate charge the thing carries (0.06-0.09 on the three authored). A relic is gathered for its charge, not worn as gear.

madeAtLevel.description: SNG-659 §2b: the level this item was MADE at — the maker's level when it was crafted, or the authored level of a relic or a legend's gear. The earned-power ceiling reads max(this, the bearer's level), so a master's artifact is strong in an apprentice's hand. Omit it and the item reads the bearer's level, which is what every item did before this field existed.
